note: NASA-recognised Earth analogue sites paired with the Analog Finder target they stand in for. Earth coordinates mark the field area (the model uses every land cell within 50 km). Pakistani twins in lib/data/twins.ts are excluded: they are TwinWorlds proposals, not NASA analogues. Where NASA names a whole region of Mars or the Moon, the pair uses the Finder target that best represents it, said in `why`.

pairs.why: Hyper-arid soils for life-detection instruments; NASA's Analog Explorer pairs it with Perseverance's search for biosignatures.
NASA astrobiology research site for dry, oxidised Mars-like soils (Curiosity's Gale crater sediments).
Used as a field analogue for the Phoenix lander: ice-cemented polar soils.
Cold desert with ground ice, compared with Mars by NASA Earth Observatory.
NASA Haughton-Mars Project: polar desert with patterned ground over permafrost.
NASA Haughton-Mars Project: cold-desert impact terrain with ground ice, like the mid-latitude northern plains.
Rocky plains like Viking 2's view of Utopia Planitia; the Mars 2020 team practised hazard avoidance here.
Perchlorate-type salts like those Phoenix found in the northern plains.
Slow-moving gravel ripples and basaltic sand, compared with Martian ripples and dunes.
Lake-edge carbonate sediments with minerals in common with Jezero crater.
Salty ancient lakebeds for studying how biosignatures survive, for Curiosity at Mount Sharp.
Arctic Mars Analogue Svalbard Expedition (AMASE) field-tested Curiosity's CheMin and SAM instruments.
NASA's MARTE drilling project in acidic, iron- and sulfate-rich ground; Mawrth Vallis is the Finder's closest sulfate- and clay-bearing target.
Phyllosilicate and sulfate soils studied by NASA Ames as analogues to Mars landing sites.
Exhumed river channels and concretions, analogues for Martian fluvial deposits.
Basalt landscapes where NASA rehearses lunar field geology.
Lava caves studied from inside and above, compared with the Marius Hills pit.
Ground-penetrating radar for buried ice, the technique planned for lunar south-pole cold traps.
NASA's 2010 and 2012 lunar ISRU field tests: prospecting for and extracting resources as at the south pole.
Basaltic tephra used as a lunar regolith analogue in the ISRU field tests.
Desert RATS Artemis simulations emulating lunar south-pole terrain and communications.
San Francisco Volcanic Field lava flow used since Apollo for lunar mission simulations.
The Haughton-Mars Project describes itself as the largest land-based Moon/Mars analogue: a cold, barren impact crater.
